goal: Fix the KitCode desktop pet so it behaves like the Codex pet: clicking the pet grabs it for drag instead of clicking through to apps behind it, dropping pins it in place, and default animation stays quiet and state-driven instead of looping arbitrary motion.

in: Make the visible pet area reliably receive mouse input so users can click and drag the pet immediately from the desktop overlay.
Remove the current mouse-ignore deadlock where the native pet window forwards events to apps behind it before the renderer can detect interactive pixels.
Prioritize Codex-like drag behavior over perfect per-pixel click-through inside the pet's tight 192x208 overlay bounds.
Keep the overlay tightly bounded to the pet asset; the desktop must remain normally clickable outside the pet window.
Keep `-webkit-app-region: drag` or equivalent native drag support so drag works without adding an in-pet command, button, or separate control surface.
After drop, keep the pet pinned at the released position for the current Terminal session and reuse that position across PET OFF/ON toggles.
Keep display workArea clamping and display-change recovery so a dragged pet cannot remain off-screen after monitor changes.
Make default animation quiet: opening may wave once, idle may blink lightly, drag/drop may show a short feedback animation, and reward-ready may celebrate.

Stop using active tracking or generic online state to loop full-body `working` animation continuously; active tracking may update a subtle face/state expression only if it does not look like arbitrary movement.
Keep summary/SSE reads and reward contracts unchanged; this requirement changes pet presentation and input behavior only.
Update focused checks so they catch click-through drag regressions, pinned drop behavior, quiet default animation policy, and no new `kitcode pet` command.
out: No new CLI command, safe-shell command, pet palette, pet marketplace, Hatch runtime dependency, or standalone pet process.
No persistent pet position across Terminal sessions; position remains session-only.
No full-screen transparent overlay and no desktop-wide input capture.
No reward math, tracker, local API response shape, persisted state, or campaign backend changes.
No attempt to guarantee perfect per-pixel click-through inside the tight pet window in this correction; that can be revisited later with native hit-test work if needed.
No redesign or regeneration of the Kit Terminal pet art unless the existing frames cannot support the needed quiet/drag feedback states.

acceptance_criteria.summary: When PET is ON, clicking the visible pet overlay starts native drag instead of activating whatever app/content is behind the pet.
After the user releases a drag, the pet remains at the dropped position, does not auto-walk away, and PET OFF/ON reuses that session position.
Only the tight pet BrowserWindow can intercept input; desktop/app interaction outside the 192x208 pet overlay remains unaffected, with no full-screen transparent capture window.

Visible pet defaults to a calm idle state with only occasional blink; opening, drag/drop, reward-ready, offline, and reconnecting states have explicit animation reasons, and active tracking no longer causes continuous arbitrary full-body looping.
The pet continues reading existing `/api/summary` and `/api/events` data without changing reward, tracker, local HTTP, or persisted state contracts.
The PET toggle remains the only control surface; no standalone `kitcode pet` command, safe-shell `pet` command, or independent pet application is introduced.

coverage_plan.summary: Update the focused pet window check to fail if the pet defaults to mouse-ignore forwarding, relies on renderer mousemove to enable first drag, loops arbitrary working animation for active tracking, or exposes a pet command.

Update the Electron-native pet harness to verify PET ON creates one bounded overlay, the pet accepts drag placement, drop pins the position, hidden pet stays pinned, and Terminal close destroys the pet.
Run the full CLI package build so terminal modes, pet assets, reward, ledger, source snapshot, command contract, and syntax checks still pass.

On macOS, run KitCode Terminal, turn PET ON, confirm clicking the pet no longer clicks the app behind it, drag/drop pins the pet, idle animation is calm, reward/offline states are explainable, and apps outside the pet overlay remain clickable.

risks.summary: Electron mouse forwarding and native drag acquisition conflict: forwarding events lets users click apps behind the pet, but it also prevents the pet renderer from receiving the first event needed to start drag.
risks.mitigation: For this correction, prioritize Codex-like drag reliability and keep the overlay tightly bounded; defer perfect per-pixel click-through inside the pet box unless native hit-test work is explicitly requested.

risks.summary: Making the pet quiet can either feel lifeless or still feel noisy if the active-tracking state loops too often.
risks.mitigation: Use idle/blink as the default, reserve stronger loops for reward-ready or explicit transient actions, and manually QA perceived motion with tracker active and inactive.

risks.summary: The Codex runner has previously timed out before Electron `app.ready`, so full native verification may still require running the harness in a normal macOS Terminal.
risks.mitigation: Keep static/build checks deterministic in CI-like contexts and document the native command for local macOS verification.

implementation_handoff.summary: Correct the pet overlay input and animation policy so the first user click grabs the pet for drag, drop pins it, and idle behavior is calm and explainable.
suggested_sequence: Change the native pet BrowserWindow input mode so the visible pet can receive the first click/drag instead of forwarding it to apps behind the pet.
Remove or simplify the renderer alpha-hit-test path if it no longer participates in first-click drag acquisition.
Keep the window size bounded to the pet dimensions and preserve session-only lastPosition reuse plus display workArea clamping.
Adjust the animation decision policy so active tracking does not continuously loop full-body working motion; default visible state should settle to idle plus occasional blink.
Update focused static and native checks for the new click/drag and quiet-animation contract, then run the package build and manual macOS QA.
current_behavior_evidence: packages/kitcode-cli/src/pet-electron.mjs currently calls `setIgnoreMouseEvents(true, {forward: true})` when the pet window is created, so the first click can pass through to the app behind the pet.

packages/kitcode-cli/src/pet-window.mjs currently tries to call `setInteractive` from `mousemove` after alpha hit-testing, but ignored mouse events can prevent that mousemove from reaching the renderer.
packages/kitcode-cli/src/pet-window.mjs currently maps active tracking summaries to `working`, which can make the pet loop motion even when the user expects it to stand still.
packages/kitcode-cli/src/pet-electron.mjs already stores `lastPosition` from native move events and can reuse that as the session-pinned drop location.
notes: This is a correction to the existing `kit-terminal-desktop-pet` work, not a new user-facing pet command or Hatch feature.
The product priority is Codex-like drag reliability. Perfect transparent-pixel pass-through inside the tight pet window is explicitly lower priority for this correction.
